stem: When counseling a kidney recipient about long-term risks of maintenance immunosuppression, which complication pair is emphasized in transplant pharmacology references?

options.text: Acute hyperkalemia and iron overload only
Immediate primary nonfunction at two years post-transplant
Permanent resolution of all pre-transplant allergies

explanation.rationale_correct: Long-term immunosuppression references emphasize opportunistic infection and malignancy among the most significant feared complications of prolonged therapy.

rationale_incorrect.B: Electrolyte and iron issues are not the primary long-term immunosuppression complication pair cited in these references.
rationale_incorrect.C: Primary nonfunction is an early graft event, not the described long-term immunosuppression risk pairing.
rationale_incorrect.D: Immunosuppression does not permanently cure pre-transplant allergic disease.

stem: A kidney recipient is eight months post-transplant with stable graft function. According to long-term follow-up references, what clinic visit interval is generally recommended through the end of the first post-transplant year?

options.text: Visits only when the recipient feels ill
No transplant center follow-up after month three

explanation.rationale_correct: Follow-up references recommend transitioning to monthly clinic visits by six months post-transplant and maintaining that monthly schedule through the end of the first year for functioning grafts.

rationale_incorrect.B: Biennial visits are far less frequent than the recommended first-year schedule.
rationale_incorrect.C: Scheduled surveillance continues even when the recipient feels well.
rationale_incorrect.D: Transplant center follow-up continues throughout the first year and beyond.

stem: A kidney recipient on discharge calls because they vomited and could not take their evening immunosuppression dose. Which instruction aligns with standard medication education?

options.text: They should understand what to do if they miss a dose or cannot take medication due to nausea or vomiting
They should permanently stop all immunosuppression after one missed dose
They should double the next dose without contacting the team
They should wait one week before reporting missed doses

explanation.rationale_correct: Discharge medication education includes teaching recipients what to do if they miss a dose or cannot take medication because of nausea, vomiting, or prolonged diarrhea.

rationale_incorrect.B: Recipients should not independently discontinue immunosuppression after vomiting; they need team guidance.
rationale_incorrect.C: Dose adjustments require coordinated medical direction, not automatic doubling.
rationale_incorrect.D: Missed doses during illness require timely team contact, not delayed reporting.
